title: Contract papers: the start date in the term clause against the meeting that approved them
question: Did the term these contracts state begin before the board meeting that approved or ratified them?
finding: 274 contract and amendment papers were read; 104 state a start date that could be read (102 as a date in the term clause, 2 as a fiscal-year term). Of the 67 first contracts among them, 35 begin before the meeting, by a median of 67 days and at most 354; the other 32 begin after it. 34 of the 37 amendments restate a start before their meeting, which is the original contract’s term, not new work begun early. 73 of the 274 say they take effect only on board approval. For 170 papers no start date could be read (scans, or forms without a term clause).
how: pdftotext -layout of each saved PDF (OCR of the first 4 and last 3 pages where there is no text layer). Start = the first date after "commence on", "Contract Dates", "effective as of" or "effective ... (Effective Date)"; failing these, 1 July of the fiscal year named where the term is "the fiscal year (July 1 to June 30)". The same paper posted twice for one meeting is counted once. Days = meeting date minus start.
limits: A start date is what the paper states, not proof that work was done that day. Afterschool agreements run with the school year and reach the board in the following weeks as a matter of calendar; an amendment repeats the original start. The papers themselves say they take effect only on approval or ratification, which the board’s rules provide for. Scans and partial uploads leave many papers without a readable term.
